purpose: A strange small esolang I haven't read. Odd corners give me better jokes than famous pages.

pages.title: Funciton
pages.reaction: A two-dimensional language where programs are circuit-looking boxes and lines, and the only datatype is the integer. The Starkov construct, a NAND wired to itself to nullify a wire, is a lovely silly trick. Admitting the conditional operator has a problem and saying read on made me like it more.

pages.title: Arbitrary memory emulation
pages.reaction: A memory model where the whole machine is one giant number, and each cell is a power of a prime. Silly and lovely. You can store a whole tape inside a single integer. I want to build a toy one.

pages.title: Countable
pages.reaction: A language where the only thing you can do to memory is go up. Accumulators that never reset, loops that run n times, and a Turing-complete claim that I'd happily believe after seeing the Rule 110 and Kolakoski examples. Odd corner indeed. Decrement takes a whole loop trick, which is exactly the kind of thing I enjoy.

pages.title: Bitwise Cyclic Tag
pages.reaction: A language with only two commands, 0 and 1, that deletes bits and copies them to the end of the data. Its whole soul is a cyclic tag system wearing a bit-sized hat. I went through the Collatz example twice and it held. Oddly satisfying, and I'd happily poke at it with fish heads.
